equivalence_tests.level: pointwise score identity at one state
equivalence_tests.sufficient: All contributing assets have same ratio s_i/g_i, or candidate support has only one effective nonnegative asset direction. One active asset is a simple sufficient case.
equivalence_tests.warning: A heterogeneous class set is not necessary: same class with different d/h, or marked/unmarked support, can give different ratios. Different classes alone are not sufficient.

equivalence_tests.condition: For each semantic-ordered candidate pair, impose the corresponding sign/tie inequalities on (a_j-a_k)+lambda*(b_j-b_k), b=F*g. Include deterministic cost/candidate-ID ordering.
equivalence_tests.warning: Nonproportional semantic/generic score vectors do not guarantee a ranking change; common terms can dominate.

equivalence_tests.condition: For S winner j, intersect lambda>=0, a_j+lambda*b_j>0, and a_j-a_k+lambda*(b_j-b_k)>=0 for all k. Use strict >0 when competitor wins cost/ID ties. If S selects none, require every a_k+lambda*b_k<=0.
equivalence_tests.criterion: Empty interval is necessary and sufficient for inability to reproduce that S selected-option decision with this nonnegative uniform generic family. It does not compare every possible geometry-only method.

equivalence_tests.level: single global weight over multiple states
equivalence_tests.condition: Intersection of all per-state intervals I_t; empty intersection rules out one constant weight across those recorded states.
equivalence_tests.warning: Each state can admit its own weight while their common interval is empty. A nonempty saved-state intersection is not an independently executed weighted rollout or held-out performance result.

identifiability_conditions: At least one nonzero contributing factor on marked support with m*v*w*d!=0; otherwise S=G=X exactly.

To escape uniform scaling within one state, candidate paths must expose distinguishable effective support mixtures and effective semantic/generic ratios; effective rank1 support always admits score scaling.
Heterogeneous ratios and support mixtures enable, but do not ensure, a selected-option witness. The exact upper-envelope/interval test must fail for a genuine witness.

Different directions matter only through actual surviving assets and outbound support factors. New heading/candidate/extent/grouping changes alter the method and cannot be introduced as implementation detail.
A coefficient-level witness is not proof the native generator can realize those candidates, nor that an unknown-coverage metric improves.
